mainTopic: Whether a טבול יום may do the פרה אדומה service, and whether an ערל may eat מעשר שני
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof from a פסוק. The word 'pure' in the sprinkling verse hints that the person is not fully pure, so a טבול יום is fit to do the פרה אדומה service. Then students ask רב ששת whether an ערל may eat מעשר שני. One side says that since פסח learns from מעשר שני about אנינות, maybe מעשר שני learns from פסח about ערלות. The other side says a stricter thing learns from a lighter one, but not the other way around. רב ששת quotes a משנה that lists rules for תרומה and ביכורים that do not apply to מעשר. He argues that if an ערל could eat מעשר, the משנה should have listed that as a difference too. The גמרא answers תנא ושייר: the list is not complete. As proof, it points to the סיפא, which also leaves out a rule: impure מעשר and ביכורים may not be burned for benefit.

steps.title: A verse shows a טבול יום may do the red heifer service
steps.stepSummary: The word 'pure' in the פסוק about sprinkling hints that this person is not fully pure. So a טבול יום is fit for the פרה אדומה service.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, "And the pure person shall sprinkle upon the impure." Why does it need to call him "pure"? That suggests he is still impure in some way. This teaches that a טבול יום is fit to do the פרה אדומה service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a proof from a פסוק. The proof shows that a טבול יום may take part in the פרה אדומה process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the sprinkler 'pure' would be unnecessary if he were completely pure. So the תורה must mean someone who is only partly pure: a טבול יום, who has gone to the מקוה but has not yet waited until nightfall. The extra word is read as the source for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who went to the מקוה today but is not fully pure until nightfall
By implication; from this we can learn
The red heifer, whose ashes are used to purify people from טומאת מת
And he shall sprinkle (the purifying water)

steps.whatToRemember: A טבול יום is fit to do the פרה אדומה service. We learn this from the extra word 'pure' (טהור) in the פסוק.

phrases.english: "And the pure person shall sprinkle upon the impure"
"Pure": by implication, he is impure (in some way)
This teaches about a טבול יום
that he is fit for the (red) heifer.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא, לִימֵּד עַל טְבוּל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a derivation that began earlier on the דף.
steps.raayaObject: That a טבול יום is fit for the פרה אדומה service
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'הטהור' in במדבר 19:19, read as implying a person who is not fully pure

steps.title: May an uncircumcised man eat second tithe?
steps.stepSummary: Students ask רב ששת whether an ערל may eat מעשר שני. They suggest it might be forbidden, because פסח already learns a rule from מעשר שני, so maybe the learning works in both directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב ששת: What is the law for an ערל regarding מעשר שני? We already learn פסח from מעשר שני about אנינות. Do we also learn מעשר שני from פסח about ערלות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its earlier discussion and opens a new question to רב ששת. Here we hear the first side of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that an אונן may not eat קרבן פסח, and we learn that from מעשר שני. The students ask whether the link works both ways. If it does, then since an ערל may not eat קרבן פסח, he would also be forbidden to eat מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked him (a question)
An uncircumcised man
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים in a state of purity
The status of a mourner on the day a close relative dies
Learns (one law from another)

phrases.english: They asked Rav Sheshet:
An uncircumcised man: what is the law regarding tithe?
phrases.notes: This is מעשר שני, the tithe the owner eats in ירושלים.

phrases.english: Just as we learn the Pesach offering from tithe
regarding acute mourning,
do we also learn tithe from the Pesach offering
regarding being uncircumcised,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the פרה אדומה derivation and returns to the earlier discussion about ערל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an ערל is forbidden to eat מעשר שני, learned from קרבן פסח

steps.title: The other side: a lighter thing does not learn from a stricter thing
steps.stepSummary: The second side of the question: maybe the stricter פסח can learn from the lighter מעשר שני, but not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps a stricter thing learns from a lighter thing, but a lighter thing does not learn from a stricter thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The students finish the question by giving the other possible side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרבן פסח is stricter than מעשר שני. If a rule applies even to the lighter מעשר שני, it surely applies to the stricter פסח. But a rule of the strict פסח, like the ban on an ערל, does not have to carry over to the lighter מעשר שני. On this side, an ערל could eat מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
Stricter, more serious
Lighter, less strict

steps.confusionAlert: This is not two separate questions. Steps 2 and 3 are the two sides of one question: does the learning go both ways, or only from the lighter thing to the stricter thing?

phrases.english: Or perhaps:
the stringent is learned from the lenient,
phrases.notes: "Stringent" means the פסח offering, and "lenient" means מעשר שני.

phrases.english: but the lenient is not learned from the stringent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question begun in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the learning only goes from the lighter thing to the stricter one, which would allow an ערל to eat מעשר שני

steps.title: רב ששת begins answering from a משנה about תרומה and ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the answer is already found in a משנה, and he starts quoting it. Both תרומה and ביכורים carry מיתה and חומש, and both are forbidden to זרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: You already learned this in a משנה. For תרומה and ביכורים, one is liable to death and to adding a fifth, and they are forbidden to non-כהנים...
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת starts his answer by quoting a משנה. Here he lists the rules that תרומה and ביכורים share. The quote continues in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת does not answer from logic. He points to a משנה (מסכת חלה) that lists rules that apply to תרומה and ביכורים but not to מעשר. His proof will not come from any rule the משנה states. It will come from the fact that the list never mentions ערל (step 6).

keyTerms.meaning: You (already) learned it, in a משנה or ברייתא
The portion of produce given to a כהן
First fruits, brought to the מקדש and given to the כהן
An added fifth, paid by a non-כהן who eats holy food by mistake
Non-כהנים

phrases.english: He said to them: You learned it:
phrases.notes: He means it's already in a משנה (חלה 1:9).

phrases.english: Teruma and first fruits
one is liable for them to death and to a fifth,
phrases.notes: "Death" means at the hands of Heaven. The fifth is added when a non-כהן eats them by mistake.

phrases.english: and they are forbidden to non-priests,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from steps 2 and 3 by pointing to a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ששת begins answering from a משנה in חלה that lists how תרומה and ביכורים differ from מעשר. He will argue that ערל is missing from that list (step 6).

steps.title: The rest of the משנה's list for תרומה and ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת finishes quoting the משנה. It lists more rules that apply to תרומה and ביכורים but not to מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They belong to the כהן as his own property. They are cancelled out in a mixture of one hundred and one. They need hand-washing, and they need sunset. All of these apply to תרומה and ביכורים, but not to מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת is still quoting the משנה he started in the last step. This is the end of its list of ways תרומה and ביכורים differ from מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists more rules where תרומה and ביכורים are stricter or different than מעשר. Then it closes with a summary line saying none of this applies to מעשר. This closing line is what רב ששת will build his proof on next.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן's own private property
They get cancelled out when mixed into one hundred times as much regular food
Washing hands before eating
Waiting for sunset after immersion before eating
Here it means מעשר שני, the second tithe eaten in ירושלים

phrases.english: And they are the property of the כהן,
and they are cancelled out in one hundred and one,
and they require washing of the hands
and sunset.
phrases.notes: A כהן who was impure and immersed still has to wait until nightfall before eating them.

phrases.english: These apply to תרומה and ביכורים,
which is not so with מעשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ בַּתְּרוּמָה וּבַבִּכּוּרִים, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּמַּעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה quote that רב ששת began in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה gives a list of differences between תרומה/ביכורים and מעשר, and that list does not mention ערל.

steps.title: רב ששת's proof: the משנה should have listed ערל
steps.stepSummary: If an ערל could eat מעשר but not תרומה, the משנה should have listed that as a difference. It did not, so an ערל must be forbidden in מעשר too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so, let the משנה teach: an ערל is forbidden to eat them, which is not so with מעשר!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת now uses the משנה to answer the students' question. He points out that the list leaves out the ערל rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ערל is definitely forbidden to eat תרומה. If he were allowed to eat מעשר, that would be one more difference, and the משנה should have listed it. Since it is missing, רב ששת concludes that an ערל is forbidden to eat מעשר too.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it were so (if your idea were true)
Let it teach (the משנה should have said)
An uncircumcised man

phrases.english: And if it is so
phrases.notes: He means: if an ערל really were allowed to eat מעשר.

phrases.english: let it teach: an ערל is forbidden to eat them,
which is not so with מעשר!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה quoted in steps 4 and 5.
steps.raayaObject: An ערל is forbidden to eat מעשר שני.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה lists differences between תרומה/ביכורים and מעשר and does not mention ערל.

steps.title: The משנה did not list everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה taught some differences and left others out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught some and left some out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת's proof. It says the missing ערל rule proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's proof only works if the משנה's list is complete. The גמרא says it is not complete. So the ערל rule could simply be one of the things the משנה left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא taught some cases and left others out

phrases.english: He taught and left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה's silence about ערל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the משנה's list is complete, but a משנה may leave items out.

steps.title: What else did the משנה leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what other item the משנה left out, which would show it also left out ערל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what else did he leave out, that you say he left out this one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer 'he left things out.' It wants a second missing item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The understood rule is that a תנא does not leave out just one item. If he skipped one, there should be another skipped item too. So to say the משנה skipped ערל, the גמרא must show something else that was also skipped.

keyTerms.meaning: What did he leave out?
That this one

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a general question about the משנה. It is a test of the answer 'he left things out,' which only holds if a second missing item can be found.

phrases.english: And what else did he leave out, that this one was left out?
phrases.notes: He means: show me one more missing item, and then I'll accept that ערל was left out too.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 7 that the משנה left items out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תנא who leaves things out does not leave out just one. If no other missing item can be found, the claim falls apart and רב ששת's proof stands.

steps.title: The next part of the משנה also leaves something out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the סיפא, which lists rules shared by מעשר and ביכורים but not תרומה. That part also has something left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He left something out, as he teaches in the latter part: There are things with מעשר and ביכורים that are not so with תרומה. מעשר and ביכורים must be brought to the place. They need a declaration. They are forbidden to an אונן, and רבי שמעון permits. They must be removed at ביעור time, and רבי שמעון exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It points to the next part of the same משנה as the place where another item was left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא gives a new list, comparing מעשר and ביכורים against תרומה. The גמרא will show in the next step that this list also leaves out a real difference. That gives two missing items, so ערל can be one of them, and רב ששת's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter part of the משנה
Bringing to the special place (ירושלים)
A formal declaration said over them
A mourner on the day a close relative died, before burial
Required removal of leftover produce at a set time

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a proof from what a משנה does not say only works if the list is complete. Showing another missing item breaks the proof.

phrases.english: He left something out, as he teaches in the latter part:
There are things with מעשר and ביכורים
which is not so with תרומה,
since מעשר and ביכורים
require bringing to the place,
phrases.notes: The place is ירושלים, where they must be eaten.

phrases.english: and require a declaration,
and are forbidden to an אונן,
and רבי שמעון permits.
And they are obligated in removal,
and רבי שמעון exempts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by pointing to another missing item in the סיפא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a second omission elsewhere in the same משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's list seemed complete, so leaving out ערל seemed to prove that an ערל may not eat מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא also leaves something out, so the משנה is not a complete list. Its silence about ערל proves nothing.

steps.title: The item the list left out: no burning when impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names a rule that applies to מעשר and ביכורים but not to תרומה: you may not burn them for benefit when they are impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also this rule: it is forbidden to burn them when they are in a state of טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names a rule that the סיפא's list does not include. This sets up its point that the משנה left this rule off its list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר and ביכורים may not be burned for benefit even after they become impure, for example using impure oil for a lamp. Impure תרומה may be burned this way. So this is a real difference between them and תרומה. In the next words the גמרא will show the משנה skipped it, which proves the משנה also could have skipped ערל.

keyTerms.meaning: but there is also / and yet; brings in an extra rule
to burn or use up; here, burning food for benefit
ritual impurity

steps.confusionAlert: The rule here is not just "don't eat it when impure." It means you may not even burn it for some benefit, like light. That is the part that is different from תרומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the גמרא can point to a real difference that the משנה did not list, then leaving ערל off the list proves nothing. That knocks down the proof from step 6.

phrases.english: But there is also: it is forbidden to burn them when impure,
phrases.notes: "Them" means מעשר and ביכורים. "Burn" here means using them up for benefit, like lighting a lamp with impure oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from step 9 by naming the exact rule in the סיפא that was left off the list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying an omitted item to show the list is not complete
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the משנה listed every difference, so leaving out ערל would mean there is no difference.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not burning מעשר and ביכורים when impure is a real difference from תרומה that the list does not include, so the list is not complete.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת tried to prove from the משנה's silence that an ערל may not eat מעשר. The גמרא answered תנא ושייר: the list is not complete. The סיפא leaves out the rule against burning impure מעשר and ביכורים, so the משנה's silence about ערל proves nothing.
